1.title: Resilient Applications and APIs
1.text: Welcome to Module two: Resilient Applications and A P Is. It covers the exam area Domain one: Development with A W S Services. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. Create and maintain fault-tolerant, resilient applications with retry and backoff and graceful degradation (one point one.three). Create, extend and maintain A P Is, including request and response transformations and validation (one point one.four). Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Domain one: Development with A W S Services (thirty percent). Exam format: fifty scored questions, multiple choice and multiple response; a score of seven hundred twenty on a scale of one hundred to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official A W S Developer Associate (D V A-C three) exam guide.

1.title: Resilience techniques
1.text: Resilience techniques. Retry with exponential backoff. Wait longer after each failure (one s, two s, four s...) so you do not flood a struggling service. Jitter. Add random delay so many clients do not retry at the same moment. Timeouts. Stop waiting after a set time so threads and connections are not held forever. Idempotency. A repeated request has the same effect as one request, so retries are safe.

1.title: Resilience techniques, continued
1.text: Resilience techniques. Graceful degradation. Keep core features working and drop optional ones (show cached data) when a dependency fails. Dead-letter queues. Park work that keeps failing instead of losing it or retrying forever. Circuit breaker. Stop calling a failing dependency for a while, then test it again.

1.title: Resilience techniques, continued
1.text: Resilience techniques. The figure shows this: Retry with exponential backoff and jitter. Exam tip: Throttled or five x x response equals retry with exponential backoff and jitter. The A W S S D Ks retry automatically with backoff; do not write an immediate retry loop.

1.title: Resilience techniques, continued
1.text: Resilience techniques. four hundred twenty-nine Too Many Requests and throttling errors are retryable; four x x validation errors are not (fix the request).

1.title: Amazon API Gateway
1.text: Amazon A P I Gateway. R E S T (representational state transfer) A P I. Full features: request validation, usage plans and A P I keys, caching, mapping templates. H T T P A P I. Cheaper and faster, simpler features, J W T authorizers. Web Socket A P I. Two-way, real-time connections.

1.title: Integration types (REST API)
1.text: Integration types (R E S T A P I). Lambda proxy. The whole request goes to Lambda; Lambda returns the whole response. Lambda (custom, non-proxy). A P I Gateway maps the request and response with mapping templates. H T T P or A W S service. Call another H T T P endpoint or an A W S A P I directly. Mock. A P I Gateway answers itself, with no backend.

1.title: Shaping and protecting requests
1.text: Shaping and protecting requests. Request validation. Check required parameters and body schema before the backend runs; rejects with four hundred. Mapping templates (Velocity Template Language). Transform request and response data. Throttling and usage plans. Limit requests per second and quotas per A P I key. Caching. Cache responses per stage for a T T L. C O R S. Allow browsers on other origins to call the A P I. Exam tip: "Reject bad input before it reaches Lambda" equals A P I Gateway request validation. "Change the shape of the request or response" equals mapping template (non-proxy integration). Exam tip: four x x validation errors are not retried unchanged; four hundred twenty-nine and five x x are retried with backoff.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A client receives throttling errors from a service during a traffic spike. What is the best client behavior? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Retry with exponential backoff and jitter. Backoff with jitter reduces load and avoids synchronized retries.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A retried request charged a customer twice. Which design property was missing? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Idempotency. An idempotent operation has the same effect when repeated.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A shop shows recommendations from a service that is down. What is the best graceful degradation? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Show the page without recommendations or with cached ones. Keep core features working and drop the optional one.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A team wants A P I Gateway to reject requests with a missing field before invoking Lambda. What should they use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Request validation with a model. Request validation checks the body schema and returns four hundred early.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A developer wants to change the Jason shape of a request before it reaches a backend, and the integration is not proxy. What fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A mapping template. Mapping templates transform the request and response in non-proxy integrations.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which A P I Gateway A P I type supports two-way real-time communication? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Web Socket A P I. Web Socket A P Is keep a two-way connection open.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does jitter add to a retry? Answer: A random delay, so clients do not retry at the same moment. Question two. What is idempotency? Answer: Repeating a request has the same effect as running it once. Question three. What does a circuit breaker do? Answer: Stops calling a failing dependency for a while, then tests again.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which A P I Gateway integration returns a response without any backend? Answer: Mock integration. Question five. What feature limits requests per A P I key? Answer: Usage plans with throttling and quotas. Question six. Which H T T P error class should not be retried unchanged? Answer: four x x validation errors (except throttling, four hundred twenty-nine).

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Retries: exponential backoff plus jitter; S D Ks do this; timeouts; idempotency. Degradation: keep core, drop optional; D L Q; circuit breaker. A P I types: R E S T (full), H T T P (cheap), Web Socket (real-time). Integrations: Lambda proxy, non-proxy with mapping templates, H T T P or A W S service, mock. Protect: request validation, throttling and usage plans, caching.
